```{r}
#| label: manuscript-objects
#| include: false

library(targets)
library(metacheck)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(ggplot2)
library(flextable)
tar_source("code/R")

# Runs the chunks of manuscript.qmd that compute numbers, so that every value below is the
# value the manuscript prints.
manuscript <- readLines("documentation/manuscript.qmd", warn = FALSE, encoding = "UTF-8")
fences <- grep("^```", manuscript)
ms <- new.env(parent = globalenv())
for (label in c("data", "license-value-check", "data-code-archiving-counts", "full-317-audit-load",
                "file-extension-counts", "readme-counts", "reproducibility-counts",
                "code-annotation-counts")) {
  from <- grep(paste0("^#\\| *label: *", label, " *$"), manuscript)
  to <- fences[fences > from][1]
  eval(parse(text = manuscript[(from + 1):(to - 1)], encoding = "UTF-8"), envir = ms)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: independent-recomputation
#| include: false

# Independent recomputation. Reads the raw files with its own code, and joins Cooper et
# al.'s rows on paper_number rather than on the corrected DOI. Two things are shared with
# the pipeline on purpose, because a copy would repeat the same rule: repo_url_platform()
# and is_institutional_figshare() label platforms, and the patterns that sort review
# comments are those of categorize_disagreement_causes().
ind <- new.env(parent = globalenv())
local({
  raw <- readRDS("data/metacheck_results.rds")
  cod <- read.csv("data/cooper_coded_data.csv")
  pap <- read.csv("data/papers_data.csv", colClasses = "character")
  cod$id <- pap$article_id[match(as.character(cod$paper_number), pap$paper_number)]
  stopifnot(!anyNA(cod$id), !anyDuplicated(cod$id))
  ids <- cod$id
  st <- raw$summary_table
  rt <- raw$repo_check$table
  sd <- raw$data_check$structure
  ct <- raw$code_check$table
  rm_ <- raw$repo_check$repo_metadata
  source("code/R/platforms.R", local = TRUE)

  master_comparison <- data.frame(article_id = ids, recorder_ID = cod$recorder_ID)
  data_rows <- sd[sd$data_type %in% "data", ]
  papers_with_data <- unique(data_rows$paper_id)
  papers_with_code <- unique(ct$paper_id)

  # Metacheck's answers, one value per paper in the order of ids.
  mc_avail <- ids %in% st$paper_id[st$files_n %in% seq_len(1e7)]
  has_license <- tapply(rm_$license, rm_$repo_url, function(v) any(!is.na(v)))
  mc_lic <- rep(NA, length(ids))
  for (i in which(ids %in% papers_with_data)) {
    u <- unique(data_rows$repo_url[data_rows$paper_id == ids[i]])
    mc_lic[i] <- any(has_license[u] %in% TRUE)
  }
  fetched <- data_rows[!is.na(data_rows$file_location) & nzchar(data_rows$file_location), ]
  mc_dl <- rep(NA, length(ids))
  for (i in which(ids %in% fetched$paper_id)) mc_dl[i] <- any(fetched$tabular_usable[fetched$paper_id == ids[i]] %in% TRUE)
  mc_code <- ids %in% papers_with_code
  mc_code_dl <- rep(NA, length(ids))
  for (i in which(mc_code)) {
    fl <- ct$file_location[ct$paper_id == ids[i]]
    mc_code_dl[i] <- any(!is.na(fl) & nzchar(fl))
  }
  mc_readme <- ids %in% rt$paper_id[rt$doc_role %in% "readme"]
  bool <- function(x, yes, no) ifelse(x %in% yes, TRUE, ifelse(x %in% no, FALSE, NA))
  c_readme_d <- bool(cod$data_README, c("Yes", "Quasi-README"), "No")
  c_readme_c <- bool(cod$code_README, c("Yes", "Quasi-README"), "No")
  c_readme <- ifelse(c_readme_d %in% TRUE | c_readme_c %in% TRUE, TRUE,
                     ifelse(is.na(c_readme_d) & is.na(c_readme_c), NA, FALSE))

  conf <- function(cb, mb) {
    ok <- !is.na(cb) & !is.na(mb); a <- cb[ok]; b <- mb[ok]
    tp <- sum(a & b); fn <- sum(a & !b); fp <- sum(!a & b); tn <- sum(!a & !b)
    mt <- suppressWarnings(mcnemar.test(matrix(c(tp, fn, fp, tn), 2)))
    list(tp = tp, fn = fn, fp = fp, tn = tn, n_both_coded = sum(ok), n_agree = tp + tn, n_disagree = fn + fp,
         pct_agree = 100 * (tp + tn) / sum(ok), sensitivity = tp / (tp + fn), specificity = tn / (tn + fp),
         ppv = tp / (tp + fp), mcnemar_stat = unname(mt$statistic), mcnemar_df = unname(mt$parameter), mcnemar_p = mt$p.value)
  }
  results <- list(
    data_availability = conf(bool(cod$data_availability, "Yes", c("No", "No, but they are available on request")), mc_avail),
    data_license = conf(bool(cod$data_license, "Yes", "No"), mc_lic),
    data_download = conf(bool(cod$data_download, c("Yes", "Yes, but not all data"), "No"), mc_dl),
    code_archived = conf(bool(cod$code_archived, "Yes", "No"), mc_code),
    code_download = conf(bool(cod$code_download, "Yes", "No"), mc_code_dl),
    any_readme = conf(c_readme, mc_readme))

  # Platform comparison, as sets, for a table of files and Cooper et al.'s column.
  plat_cmp <- function(tab, coded) {
    gh <- "github, gitlab, codeberg or similar platform"; oth <- "other repo/database"
    one <- vector("list", length(ids)); cats <- rep(NA_character_, length(ids)); found <- rep(NA_character_, length(ids))
    sets <- split(tab$repo_url[!is.na(tab$repo_url) & nzchar(tab$repo_url)], tab$paper_id[!is.na(tab$repo_url) & nzchar(tab$repo_url)])
    for (i in seq_along(ids)) {
      u <- unique(sets[[ids[i]]])
      if (is.na(coded[i]) || !length(u)) next
      a <- unique(tolower(trimws(strsplit(coded[i], ";")[[1]])))
      a[a == "cran"] <- oth
      a <- unique(setdiff(a, c("supplementary materials", "personal website")))
      lab <- repo_url_platform(u)
      b <- tolower(lab); b[b == "osf"] <- oth
      fig <- u[lab == "Figshare"]
      if (length(fig) && all(is_institutional_figshare(fig)) && "figshare" %in% b && !"figshare" %in% a && oth %in% a) b[b == "figshare"] <- oth
      b <- unique(b)
      if (!length(a)) next
      cats[i] <- if (setequal(a, b)) "exact" else if (all(b %in% a)) "mc_fewer" else if (all(a %in% b)) "mc_more" else if (any(a %in% b)) "partial" else "none"
      if (all(c(gh, "zenodo") %in% a)) found[i] <- if (all(c(gh, "zenodo") %in% b)) "both" else if (gh %in% b) "github_only" else if ("zenodo" %in% b) "zenodo_only" else "neither"
      one[[i]] <- length(a)
    }
    k <- table(factor(cats, c("exact", "mc_fewer", "mc_more", "partial", "none")))
    list(categories = k, category = cats, n_both_coded = sum(!is.na(cats)), n_agree = unname(k["exact"]),
         pct_agree = 100 * unname(k["exact"]) / sum(!is.na(cats)), n_any_overlap = sum(cats != "none", na.rm = TRUE),
         pct_any_overlap = 100 * mean(cats[!is.na(cats)] != "none"), n_cooper_multi = sum(unlist(one) > 1),
         n_cooper_github_zenodo = sum(!is.na(found)), github_zenodo = table(factor(found, c("both", "github_only", "zenodo_only", "neither"))),
         github_zenodo_found = found)
  }
  results$data_archive <- plat_cmp(data_rows, cod$data_archive)
  results$code_archive <- plat_cmp(ct, cod$code_archive)

  # The review file itself.
  rv <- openxlsx::read.xlsx("data/review/disagreement_review_data.xlsx")
  verdict_tallies <- lapply(setNames(nm = c("data_availability", "data_license", "data_download", "code_archived", "code_download", "any_readme")),
                            function(k) table(rv[[paste0(k, "_verdict")]]))
  cooper_right_causes <- categorize_disagreement_causes(rv)$cooper_right_causes
  n_review <- nrow(rv)
  vcols <- paste0(c("data_availability", "data_archive", "data_license", "data_download", "code_archived", "code_archive", "code_download", "any_readme"), "_verdict")
  n_reviewed <- sum(rowSums(!is.na(rv[vcols])) > 0)
  Review_status <- sprintf("All %d disagreeing papers carry a verdict for every column on which they disagree", n_review)
  cause_of <- function(col) { cm <- rv[[paste0(col, "_comment")]]; ifelse(grepl("CAUSE: ", cm, fixed = TRUE), sub("^.*CAUSE: ([A-Z_]+).*$", "\\1", cm), NA) }
  n_cause <- function(col, cause, verdict = c("COOPER_RIGHT", "METACHECK_RIGHT", "BOTH_DEFENSIBLE")) sum(cause_of(col) %in% cause & rv[[paste0(col, "_verdict")]] %in% verdict)
  code_categories <- rv[!is.na(rv$code_category), c("code_category", "code_category_reason", "code_archived_verdict")]
  n_code <- function(category) sum(code_categories$code_category == category)
  n_code_reason <- function(text) sum(grepl(text, code_categories$code_category_reason, fixed = TRUE))
  n_dl_right <- function(pattern) sum(rv$data_download_verdict %in% "COOPER_RIGHT" & grepl(pattern, rv$data_download_comment, perl = TRUE))
  rv_readme <- c_readme[match(rv$article_id, ids)] %in% TRUE
  n_readme <- function(cooper_yes, verdict) sum(rv_readme == cooper_yes & rv$any_readme_verdict %in% verdict)
  n_readme_description <- sum(rv_readme & rv$any_readme_verdict %in% "DIFFERENT_DEFINITION" & grepl("landing page|description|abstract", rv$any_readme_comment, ignore.case = TRUE))
  n_readme_in_archive <- sum(rv$any_readme_verdict %in% "COOPER_RIGHT" & grepl("README is inside|README sits inside|tar archive|\\.rar|\\.7z|ZIP64", rv$any_readme_comment))
  un <- is.na(c_readme)
  n_readme_uncoded <- sum(un)
  n_readme_uncoded_unsure <- sum(un & (cod$data_README %in% "Unsure" | cod$code_README %in% "Unsure"))
  n_readme_uncoded_archived <- sum(un & (cod$data_availability %in% "Yes" | cod$code_archived %in% "Yes"))

  # Open data and code as judged from the text.
  odd_d <- st$data_open.oddpub[match(ids, st$paper_id)]; odd_c <- st$code_open.oddpub[match(ids, st$paper_id)]
  op_d <- st$data_open[match(ids, st$paper_id)]; op_c <- st$code_open[match(ids, st$paper_id)]
  acc <- function(p, t) {
    ok <- !is.na(p) & !is.na(t); p <- p[ok]; t <- t[ok]
    list(n = sum(ok), n_negative = sum(!t), n_positive = sum(t),
         n_agree = sum(p == t), n_disagree = sum(p != t),
         # the tool judged open where the coder did not, and the reverse
         n_tool_open_cooper_not = sum(p & !t), n_tool_not_cooper_open = sum(!p & t),
         sensitivity = sum(p & t) / sum(t), specificity = sum(!p & !t) / sum(!t), accuracy = mean(p == t))
  }
  td <- bool(cod$data_open, c("Yes", "Yes, but not all files"), "No"); tc <- bool(cod$code_open, "Yes", "No")
  accuracy_summary <- list(oddpub_data = acc(odd_d, td), oddpub_code = acc(odd_c, tc), metacheck_data = acc(op_d, td), metacheck_code = acc(op_c, tc))
  bd <- is.na(cod$data_open) & cod$data_availability %in% "Yes"; ad <- cod$data_open %in% "Needs specific software or too large"
  bc <- is.na(cod$code_open) & cod$code_archived %in% "Yes"; ac <- cod$code_open %in% "Maybe if I had the right software"
  n_blank_data_open <- sum(bd); n_oddpub_open_blank_data <- sum(odd_d[bd]); n_mc_open_blank_data <- sum(op_d[bd])
  n_ambig_data_open <- sum(ad); n_oddpub_open_ambig_data <- sum(odd_d[ad]); n_mc_open_ambig_data <- sum(op_d[ad])
  n_blank_code_open <- sum(bc); n_oddpub_open_blank_code <- sum(odd_c[bc]); n_mc_open_blank_code <- sum(op_c[bc])
  n_ambig_code_open <- sum(ac); n_oddpub_open_ambig_code <- sum(odd_c[ac]); n_mc_open_ambig_code <- sum(op_c[ac])

  # Papers with data or code, for each side.
  c_either <- ids[cod$data_availability %in% "Yes" | cod$code_archived %in% "Yes"]
  m_either <- union(papers_with_data, papers_with_code)
  n_cooper_data <- sum(cod$data_availability %in% "Yes"); n_cooper_code <- sum(cod$code_archived %in% "Yes"); n_cooper_either <- length(c_either)
  n_mc_repo_found <- sum(mc_avail); n_mc_data <- length(papers_with_data); n_mc_code <- length(papers_with_code); n_mc_either <- length(m_either)
  n_both_yes_either <- length(intersect(c_either, m_either)); n_cooper_yes_mc_no <- length(setdiff(c_either, m_either)); n_mc_yes_cooper_no <- length(setdiff(m_either, c_either))
  n_either_total_disagree <- n_cooper_yes_mc_no + n_mc_yes_cooper_no

  # Repositories Metacheck supports. The hosts of the Figshare family are the values of
  # .figshare_doi_prefix_hosts(); its names are DOI prefixes, not hosts.
  ns <- asNamespace("metacheck")
  dv <- union(ns$.dataverse_hosts(), names(ns$.dataverse_doi_prefix_hosts())); d7 <- ns$.dspace7_hosts(); dl <- ns$.dspace_legacy_hosts()
  dn <- vapply(ns$.dataone_hosts(), `[[`, "", "host"); fg <- union(ns$.figshare_vanity_hosts(), unlist(ns$.figshare_doi_prefix_hosts()))
  n_dataverse_hosts <- length(dv); n_dspace7_hosts <- length(d7); n_dspace_legacy_hosts <- length(dl); n_dataone_hosts <- length(dn); n_figshare_hosts <- length(fg)
  platforms <- c("researchdata4tu", "aspredicted", "dryad", "fsd", "github", "gitlab", "mendeley", "osf", "rbox", "reshare", "zenodo")
  n_dedicated_platforms <- sum(vapply(platforms, function(p) any(grepl(paste0("^\\.?", p, "(_[a-z]+)?_(links|info|files)$"), ls(ns, all.names = TRUE))), TRUE))
  n_unique_repos <- length(unique(c(dv, d7, dl, dn, fg))) + n_dedicated_platforms

  # The audit of the papers Metacheck missed.
  aud <- read.csv("data/review/manual_repo_findability_audit_data.csv"); fair <- read.csv("data/review/manual_fair_api_findability_audit_data.csv")
  rc <- aud$root_cause_category; n_rc <- function(...) sum(rc %in% c(...))
  n_no_repo_cited <- n_rc("NO_REPOSITORY_CITED"); n_nonfair_private_link <- n_rc("NOT_FAIR_PRIVATE_LINK"); n_nonfair_no_deposit <- n_rc("PLATFORM_URL_NOT_A_SINGLE_REPO")
  n_nonfair_blocked <- n_rc("NOT_FAIR_BLOCKS_AUTOMATED_ACCESS"); n_not_live <- n_rc("REPO_NOT_ACTUALLY_LIVE_OR_ACCESSIBLE"); n_nonfair_no_api <- n_rc("NOT_FAIR_NO_DATA_API")
  ff <- as.character(fair$fair_machine_findable_in_principle)
  n_unsupported_not_fair <- sum(rc == "PLATFORM_NOT_SUPPORTED" & ff == "FALSE"); n_unsupported_but_fair <- sum(rc == "PLATFORM_NOT_SUPPORTED" & ff == "TRUE")
  n_nonfair <- n_nonfair_private_link + n_nonfair_no_deposit + n_nonfair_blocked + n_not_live + n_nonfair_no_api + n_unsupported_not_fair
  n_not_fair_format <- n_rc("DATA_OR_CODE_NOT_IN_FAIR_FORMAT"); n_not_classified <- n_not_fair_format + n_rc("CLASSIFIER_EXTENSION_GAP", "CLASSIFIER_MISTYPED")
  n_lim_doi_garbled <- n_rc("EXTRACTION_GAP_DOI_GARBLED"); n_lim_text_missing <- n_rc("EXTRACTION_GAP_TEXT_MISSING"); n_lim_extraction <- n_lim_doi_garbled + n_lim_text_missing
  n_lim_code <- n_rc("SUPPORTED_PLATFORM_BUG", "CLASSIFIER_ARCHIVE_NOT_EXPANDED", "FILES_NOT_ENUMERATED"); n_metacheck_limitation <- n_lim_extraction + n_lim_code
  rl <- aud$doi_only_in_reference_list; n_lim_ref_only <- sum(!is.na(rl)); n_lim_ref_citation <- sum(rl %in% "data citation"); n_lim_ref_conversion <- sum(rl %in% "text conversion")
  n_not_fair_total <- n_no_repo_cited + n_not_fair_format + n_nonfair; n_cooper_fair <- n_cooper_either - n_not_fair_total
  pct_fair_found <- sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * n_both_yes_either / n_cooper_fair)

  # Platform section.
  n_data_mc_more_github <- { k <- results$data_archive$category %in% "mc_more"; plat <- tapply(data_rows$repo_url, data_rows$paper_id, function(u) any(repo_url_platform(unique(u)) == "GitHub, GitLab, Codeberg or similar platform"))
    sum(k & plat[ids] %in% TRUE & !grepl("GitHub", cod$data_archive, fixed = TRUE)) }
  own <- read.csv("data/review/github_repository_ownership_review_data.csv"); third <- own[!own$owner_is_author, ]
  is3 <- function(p, u) paste(p, u) %in% paste(third$article_id, third$repo_url)
  tp <- list(n_github_repos = nrow(own), n_third_party_repos = nrow(third), n_third_party_papers = length(unique(third$article_id)),
             n_corpus_papers = length(unique(third$article_id[grepl("text corpus", third$why_not_authors, fixed = TRUE)])))
  cpapers <- unique(third$article_id)
  k3 <- ct[ct$paper_id %in% cpapers, ]; only_code <- vapply(split(k3, k3$paper_id), function(d) all(is3(d$paper_id, d$repo_url)), TRUE)
  only_code <- names(only_code)[only_code]; cc3 <- cod$code_archived[match(only_code, ids)]
  tp$n_code_archived_only_third_party <- length(only_code)
  tp$code_archived_only_third_party <- c(No = sum(cc3 %in% "No"), Yes = sum(cc3 %in% "Yes"))
  f3 <- rt[rt$paper_id %in% cpapers, ]; only_any <- vapply(split(f3, f3$paper_id), function(d) all(is3(d$paper_id, d$repo_url)), TRUE); only_any <- names(only_any)[only_any]
  da3 <- cod$data_availability[match(only_any, ids)]; tp$data_availability_only_third_party <- c(Yes = sum(da3 %in% "Yes"), No = sum(da3 %in% "No"))
  without <- function(tab, coded, cats) {
    keep <- tab[!is3(tab$paper_id, tab$repo_url), ]; c2 <- plat_cmp(keep, coded)$category; list(a = cats, b = c2)
  }
  dd <- without(data_rows, cod$data_archive, results$data_archive$category); cc_ <- without(ct, cod$code_archive, results$code_archive$category)
  tp$n_data_archive_mc_more_to_exact <- sum(ids %in% cpapers & dd$a %in% "mc_more" & dd$b %in% "exact")
  tp$n_code_archive_mc_more_to_exact <- sum(ids %in% cpapers & cc_$a %in% "mc_more" & cc_$b %in% "exact")
  tp$n_code_archive_exact_only_third_party <- sum(ids %in% cpapers & cc_$a %in% "exact" & is.na(cc_$b))

  none_review <- read.csv("data/review/data_archive_no_shared_platform_review_data.csv"); gz_review <- read.csv("data/review/code_archive_github_zenodo_review_data.csv")
  none_n <- function(group) sum(none_review$group %in% group)
  nm <- none_review[!is.na(none_review$missed_cause), ]; nc <- function(cs, f = NULL) sum(nm$missed_cause %in% cs & (is.null(f) | as.character(nm$fair_machine_findable_in_principle) %in% f))
  none_not_fair <- nc("DATA_OR_CODE_NOT_IN_FAIR_FORMAT") + nc("PLATFORM_NOT_SUPPORTED", "FALSE"); none_unsupported_fair <- nc("PLATFORM_NOT_SUPPORTED", "TRUE")
  none_unsupported_format <- nc(c("CLASSIFIER_EXTENSION_GAP", "CLASSIFIER_MISTYPED")); none_limitation <- nc(c("EXTRACTION_GAP_DOI_GARBLED", "EXTRACTION_GAP_TEXT_MISSING", "SUPPORTED_PLATFORM_BUG", "CLASSIFIER_ARCHIVE_NOT_EXPANDED", "FILES_NOT_ENUMERATED"))
  gz_n <- function(category, missed = c("GitHub", "Zenodo")) sum(gz_review$category == category & gz_review$platform_missed %in% missed)

  # Downloads.
  yes_dl <- cod$data_download %in% c("Yes", "Yes, but not all data")
  n_dl_cooper_yes <- sum(yes_dl); n_dl_mc_true <- sum(yes_dl & mc_dl %in% TRUE); n_dl_mc_na <- sum(yes_dl & is.na(mc_dl))

  # Licences on Dryad.
  rmeta <- tapply(rm_$license, rm_$repo_url, function(v) if (all(is.na(v))) NA_character_ else v[!is.na(v)][1])
  pre <- paste(gsub(".", "\\.", ns$.dryad_doi_prefixes(), fixed = TRUE), collapse = "|")
  is_dry <- grepl(paste0("datadryad\\.org|(", pre, ")/dryad|doi\\.org/(", pre, ")"), names(rmeta), ignore.case = TRUE)
  cc0_url <- "https://spdx.org/licenses/CC0-1.0.html"
  n_dryad_licensed <- sum(is_dry & !is.na(rmeta)); n_dryad_cc0 <- sum(is_dry & rmeta %in% cc0_url); n_nondryad_cc0 <- sum(!is_dry & rmeta %in% cc0_url)

  rpkg <- c("10_1111_2041_210x_13750", "10_1111_1365_2664_13806", "10_1111_2041_210x_12989", "10_1111_2041_210x_13029", "10_1111_2041_210x_13503", "10_1111_2041_210x_14252", "10_1111_2041_210x_12774", "10_1111_2041_210x_14427", "10_1111_1365_2664_13795", "10_1111_2041_210x_14148", "10_1111_2041_210x_13170", "10_1111_2041_210x_12784", "10_1111_2041_210x_13009", "10_1111_2041_210x_14417", "10_1111_1365_2435_13455", "10_1111_1365_2435_14552")
  n_rpkg16_resolved <- sum(rpkg %in% papers_with_code)

  # Comment density against Cooper et al.'s rating.
  s_ok <- !is.na(ct$comment_lines) & !is.na(ct$code_lines)
  a <- aggregate(cbind(comment_lines, code_lines) ~ paper_id, ct[s_ok, ], sum); a$pct <- a$comment_lines / (a$comment_lines + a$code_lines)
  sc <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(cod$code_annotation_scale)); j <- match(a$paper_id, ids); keep <- !is.na(sc[j]) & !is.na(a$pct)
  x_ <- sc[j][keep]; b_ <- a[keep, ]
  pe <- cor.test(x_, b_$pct); sp <- suppressWarnings(cor.test(x_, b_$pct, method = "spearman")); sl <- suppressWarnings(cor.test(x_, b_$comment_lines, method = "spearman")); sk <- suppressWarnings(cor.test(b_$code_lines, b_$pct, method = "spearman"))
  cq <- list(n_both = sum(keep), n_cooper_coded = sum(!is.na(sc)), n_mc_has_stats = nrow(a), pearson_r = unname(pe$estimate), pearson_ci = pe$conf.int, pearson_p = pe$p.value,
             spearman_rho = unname(sp$estimate), spearman_p = sp$p.value, spearman_rho_lines = unname(sl$estimate), spearman_p_lines = sl$p.value, codelines_vs_pct_rho = unname(sk$estimate), codelines_vs_pct_p = sk$p.value)

  # What the modules report beyond the comparison.
  uniq <- function(v) length(unique(v)); n_f <- nrow(ct); n_p <- uniq(ct$paper_id)
  miss <- ct$loaded_files_missing %in% seq_len(1e6); abs_ <- ct$code_abs_path %in% TRUE; swd <- ct$code_setwd %in% TRUE

```{r}
#| label: number-register
#| include: false

# Every inline expression of the manuscript, evaluated with the manuscript's own objects
# and with the independent ones.
in_chunk <- (cumsum(grepl("^```", manuscript)) %% 2 == 1) | grepl("^```", manuscript)
yaml_end <- which(manuscript == "---")[2]
section <- character(length(manuscript)); current <- "Front matter"
for (i in seq_along(manuscript)) {
  if (!in_chunk[i] && i > yaml_end && grepl("^#{1,4} ", manuscript[i])) current <- sub("^#+ ", "", manuscript[i])
  section[i] <- current
}
inline_pattern <- "`r [^`]+`"
show <- function(e, env) tryCatch(paste(format(eval(parse(text = e), envir = env)), collapse = " "), error = function(err) NA_character_)
register <- do.call(rbind, lapply(which(!in_chunk & seq_along(manuscript) > yaml_end), function(i) {
  m <- gregexpr(inline_pattern, manuscript[i], perl = TRUE)[[1]]
  if (m[1] < 0) return(NULL)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(m), function(k) {
    e <- substr(manuscript[i], m[k] + 3, m[k] + attr(m, "match.length")[k] - 2)
    before <- gsub(inline_pattern, "#", substr(manuscript[i], 1, m[k] - 1), perl = TRUE)
    before <- substr(before, max(1, nchar(before) - 70), nchar(before))
    data.frame(line = i, section = section[i], expr = e, before = before, value = show(e, ms), independent = show(e, ind))
  }))
}))
same <- function(a, b) a == b | (suppressWarnings(as.numeric(a)) == suppressWarnings(as.numeric(b))) %in% TRUE
register$same <- same(register$value, register$independent)

esc <- function(x) {
  x <- gsub("`", "", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("[\r\n]+", " ", x)
  x <- gsub("\\$\\\\chi\\^2\\$", "chi-squared", x)
  x <- gsub("([\\\\*_|$%#&~^<>@\\[\\]{}])", "\\\\\\1", x, perl = TRUE)
  gsub("\\\\([~^])", "", x)
}
md_table <- function(df, widths) {
  head <- paste0("| ", paste(names(df), collapse = " | "), " |")
  rule <- paste0("|", paste(strrep("-", widths), collapse = "|"), "|")
  rows <- apply(df, 1, function(r) paste0("| ", paste(r, collapse = " | "), " |"))
  cat("", head, rule, rows, "", sep = "\n")
}
# Sections already shown by a num_table() call, so the completeness table at
# the end can list every section that was not shown by hand.
shown_sections <- character(0)
render_rows <- function(r) {
  md_table(data.frame(Line = r$line, `Text before the number` = paste0("...", esc(r$before)),
                      Manuscript = esc(r$value), Recomputed = esc(r$independent),
                      Status = ifelse(r$same %in% TRUE, "Same", "**Differs**"), check.names = FALSE),
           c(5, 54, 14, 14, 11))
}
num_table <- function(sec) {
  shown_sections <<- union(shown_sections, sec)
  r <- register[register$section == sec, ]
  if (nrow(r) == 0) {
    cat("\n*No computed numbers under a manuscript heading named \"", sec, "\".*\n", sep = "")
    return(invisible())
  }
  render_rows(r)
}
# Every register row whose section was not already shown by a num_table() call
# above, so that no computed number in the manuscript escapes this audit even
# when a heading is renamed or a section is added.
remaining_tables <- function() {
  rest <- register[!register$section %in% shown_sections, ]
  if (nrow(rest) == 0) {
    cat("\n*Every computed number is listed under one of the headings above.*\n")
    return(invisible())
  }
  for (sec in unique(rest$section)) {
    cat("\n### ", sec, "\n", sep = "")
    render_rows(rest[rest$section == sec, ])
  }
}

# Purpose and method

This document records, for the manuscript "Automatically Identifying FAIR Data and Code Sharing Practices with Metacheck" (titled "Automating Data- and Code-Archiving Checks with Metacheck" until 10 November 2026), where each number comes from and whether each factual statement is accurate. It has two parts. Part 1 is a register of numbers. Part 2 is a register of factual statements. It replaces `numbers_audit.md` of the earlier repository (Lakens/cooper-bes-validation) and keeps that file's fields: the location of a number, what it means, the chain of files that produce it, the formula, and how to read it. The checks and explanations were produced by Claude (Anthropic's AI model, Opus 5.5) at the request of Daniël Lakens, and have not yet been reviewed by a person.

```{r}
#| label: state
#| include: false

verified_md5 <- "68f5d1969b9802334359309e96a5c2ed"
current_md5 <- unname(tools::md5sum("documentation/manuscript.qmd"))
targets::tar_load(metacheck_sha, store = "_targets")
state_note <- if (identical(current_md5, verified_md5)) {
  "The manuscript file is unchanged since this verification, so the line numbers in this document are correct."
} else {
  "**The manuscript file has changed since this verification.** The tables of Part 1 show the current text and values, and the status tables in the Summary of results show where each statement of Part 2 is now and whether it has been resolved. The line numbers and quotations inside the written entries of Part 2 are those of 1 November 2026."
}
```

**State of the documents.** The verification was carried out on 1 November 2026, on commit `a704280` of Lakens/bes_validation, plus the reclassification of the README disagreements made later that day, with results produced by Metacheck 0.4.2.1 at commit `r substr(metacheck_sha, 1, 8)`. It was updated on 10 November 2026: the independent recomputation was extended to every section of the revised manuscript (including the reproducibility check, which uses its own later run), the table of typed numbers was brought up to date, and the status of each statement is now established at every render. `r state_note` Values in the tables are computed each time this document is rendered. Values in the written explanations were measured on that date. This document is not part of the pipeline in `_targets.R`; render it with `quarto::quarto_render("documentation/manuscript_verification.qmd")` after running the pipeline.

**How the numbers were checked.** A number in the manuscript is either computed by code when the manuscript is rendered, or typed by hand. For each computed number, this document takes the exact expression from the manuscript and evaluates it twice: once with the objects the manuscript uses, which the pipeline produces, and once with objects recomputed here by separately written code from the raw files `data/metacheck_results.rds`, `data/cooper_coded_data.csv`, `data/papers_data.csv` and the review files. The recomputation joins Cooper et al.'s rows to papers by their paper number, whereas the pipeline joins on a corrected DOI, so it also tests that correction. Two things are shared with the pipeline, because a copy would only repeat the same rule: the functions that assign a platform to an address (`repo_url_platform()`, `is_institutional_figshare()`), and the text patterns that sort review comments into causes. Agreement therefore shows that a number follows correctly from the files. It does not show that a human judgement stored in a review file is correct; Part 2 examines those judgements.

**How the statements were checked.** Each statement was tested against the most direct evidence available: the data, the review files, the code of the Metacheck version that was run (version 0.4.2.1, read from the installed package), the cited source, or a live request to the service concerned. The evidence used is named in each entry. Cooper et al. (2026) was read in full in the published version. Several other cited pages refused automated access, and the entries concerned say so; they are the BES author guidelines, the article by Obels et al. and the report by Vilhuber and Cavanagh.

**Verdicts.** Every statement in Part 2 carries one verdict.

- **TRUE**: the evidence supports the statement as written.
- **QUALIFIED**: the statement is correct in substance, but as written it is imprecise or incomplete in a way a reader could be misled by. The entry says what to change.
- **FALSE**: the evidence contradicts the statement, or the statement describes something that no longer exists. The entry gives the root of the error and a correction.
- **UNVERIFIED**: the statement could not be tested. The entry says what would settle it.
- **JUDGEMENT**: the statement is an evaluation or a prediction rather than a fact. The entry gives the facts it rests on.

```{r}
#| label: verdict-counts
#| include: false

self <- readLines("documentation/manuscript_verification.qmd", warn = FALSE, encoding = "UTF-8")
entry <- grepl("^\\*\\*C[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+ — (TRUE|QUALIFIED|FALSE|UNVERIFIED|JUDGEMENT)\\.\\*\\*", self)
verdict <- sub("^\\*\\*C[0-9.]+ — ([A-Z]+)\\..*$", "\\1", self[entry])
entry_id <- sub("^\\*\\*(C[0-9.]+) — .*$", "\\1", self[entry])
entry_text <- sub("^\\*\\*C[0-9.]+ — [A-Z]+\\.\\*\\* *", "", self[entry])
counts <- table(factor(verdict, c("TRUE", "QUALIFIED", "FALSE", "UNVERIFIED", "JUDGEMENT")))
n_same <- sum(register$same %in% TRUE)
differ <- register[!(register$same %in% TRUE), , drop = FALSE]
differ_lines <- if (nrow(differ)) paste(sort(unique(differ$line)), collapse = ", ") else ""

# Where each entry's quotation is in the current manuscript. The entries quote the text
# of 1 November 2026; this searches the source (outside code) and the rendered PDF, so
# that quotations holding computed numbers are found too.
norm_txt <- function(x) {
  x <- gsub("[“”]", "\"", x)
  x <- gsub("[‘’]", "'", x)
  x <- gsub("[`*_]", "", x)
  gsub("[[:space:]]+", " ", x)
}
ms_norm <- norm_txt(manuscript)
pdf_norm <- if (file.exists("documentation/manuscript.pdf")) {
  p <- paste(pdftools::pdf_text("documentation/manuscript.pdf"), collapse = "\n")
  p <- gsub("-\n[[:space:]]*", "", p)
  norm_txt(gsub("ﬁ", "fi", gsub("ﬂ", "fl", p)))
} else ""
locate <- function(x) {
  q <- regmatches(x, regexpr("\"[^\"]{12,}\"", x))
  fr <- if (length(q)) trimws(strsplit(gsub("^\"|\"$", "", q), "[.][.][.]|…")[[1]]) else character(0)
  fr <- norm_txt(gsub("^[(]|[)]$", "", fr))
  fr <- fr[nchar(fr) >= 15]
  if (!length(fr)) return(c("No quotation", "unknown"))
  hit <- unique(unlist(lapply(fr, function(f) which(!in_chunk & grepl(f, ms_norm, fixed = TRUE)))))
  found <- vapply(fr, function(f) any(grepl(f, ms_norm, fixed = TRUE)) || grepl(f, pdf_norm, fixed = TRUE), TRUE)
  where <- if (length(hit)) paste(ifelse(hit <= yaml_end, "Abstract", paste("Line", hit)), collapse = ", ") else if (any(found)) "In the text" else "Not in the text"
  c(where, if (all(found)) "all" else if (any(found)) "part" else "none")
}
loc <- t(vapply(entry_text, locate, c("", ""), USE.NAMES = FALSE))

# Entries whose statement was removed from the manuscript after 1 November 2026. Each was
# checked on 10 November 2026 by searching the manuscript for the words that carry its claim.
removed_checked <- c("C1.7", "C1.10", "C4.10", "C8.3", "C8.4", "C8.5", "C8.7", "C8.8", "C8.9", "C8.10",
                     "C9.1", "C9.3", "C9.7", "C9.8", "C9.10", "C9.12", "C10.2", "C10.3", "C10.4", "C10.7",
                     "C10.8", "C10.10", "C11.3", "C11.6", "C11.7", "C11.8", "C12.3", "C12.7", "C12.8", "C12.10",
                     "C12.11", "C12.13", "C15.4", "C15.9", "C16.1", "C16.3", "C16.5", "C16.9", "C16.11", "C17.1",
                     "C17.2", "C18.1", "C18.3", "C18.5", "C19.1", "C19.2", "C19.3", "C19.5")
decided <- rbind(decided, data.frame(id = setdiff(removed_checked, decided$id), status = "Statement removed",
  note = "The statement is no longer in the manuscript (checked on 10 November 2026 by searching for the words that carry its claim)."))
issue <- verdict %in% c("FALSE", "QUALIFIED", "UNVERIFIED")
section_removed <- sub("[.].*$", "", entry_id) %in% c("C13", "C14")
entry_status <- ifelse(entry_id %in% decided$id, decided$status[match(entry_id, decided$id)],
                ifelse(section_removed, "Section removed",
                ifelse(loc[, 2] == "none", "Text removed or rewritten",
                ifelse(loc[, 2] == "unknown", "Check by hand", "Open"))))
entry_note <- ifelse(entry_id %in% decided$id, decided$note[match(entry_id, decided$id)],
              ifelse(section_removed, "The section was removed from the manuscript.",
              ifelse(loc[, 2] == "none", "The quoted words are no longer in the manuscript; the new wording was not checked again.",
              ifelse(loc[, 2] == "part", "Part of the quoted words are still in the manuscript.",
              ifelse(loc[, 2] == "unknown", "The entry quotes no words that can be searched for.",
                     "The quoted words are still in the manuscript.")))))
status_levels <- c("Open", "Partly resolved", "Check by hand", "Resolved", "Author's decision", "Statement removed", "Section removed", "Text removed or rewritten")
status_counts <- table(factor(entry_status[issue], status_levels))
n_issue <- sum(issue)
n_still_open <- sum(status_counts[c("Open", "Partly resolved", "Check by hand")])
status_table <- function(keep) {
  k <- issue & entry_status %in% keep
  if (!any(k)) {
    cat("\n*None.*\n")
    return(invisible())
  }
  md_table(data.frame(Entry = entry_id[k], Verdict = verdict[k], `Where now` = loc[k, 1],
                      Status = paste0("**", entry_status[k], ".** ", esc(entry_note[k])), check.names = FALSE),
           c(7, 17, 14, 58))
}
# An entry has one row in decided; a second row for the same entry would be ignored.
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(decided$id))
```

# Summary of results

**Numbers.** The manuscript computes `r nrow(register)` numbers in its text. Of these, `r n_same` are reproduced by the independent recomputation, and `r nrow(register) - n_same` differ`r if (nchar(differ_lines)) paste0(" (on manuscript line(s) ", differ_lines, ")") else ""`. Each differing number is shown with its recomputed value, marked **Differs**, in the register tables of Part 1 below. The count of repositories Metacheck supports differed until 10 November 2026, because the manuscript's code counted the DOI prefixes of Figshare-based repositories as if they were hosts (76 and 285 instead of 41 and 250); the code was corrected then (entry C4.19). Part 1 also lists the typed numbers, and those that could not be traced. This summary paragraph was written for the 1 November 2026 state of the manuscript; the counts in it are recomputed on each render, but the narrative explanation of a specific difference may be out of date if the manuscript has since changed.

**Statements.** Part 2 contains `r length(verdict)` entries, with the verdicts given on 1 November 2026: `r counts[["TRUE"]]` TRUE, `r counts[["QUALIFIED"]]` QUALIFIED, `r counts[["FALSE"]]` FALSE, `r counts[["UNVERIFIED"]]` UNVERIFIED and `r counts[["JUDGEMENT"]]` JUDGEMENT.

**Status of the statements on `r format(Sys.Date(), "%d %B %Y")`.** The manuscript was revised after 1 November 2026, so the status of each entry judged FALSE, QUALIFIED or UNVERIFIED is established again at every render: its quotation is searched for in the current manuscript, and what was decided or changed for it is recorded. Of these `r n_issue` entries, `r status_counts[["Resolved"]]` are resolved by a change to the text, `r status_counts[["Author's decision"]]` were settled by a decision of the author, `r status_counts[["Statement removed"]]` concern statements that were removed from the text, `r status_counts[["Section removed"]]` belong to sections that were removed, and for `r status_counts[["Text removed or rewritten"]]` the quoted words are no longer in the manuscript, but the new wording was not checked again. `r n_still_open` `r if (n_still_open == 1) "remains" else "remain"` open: their quoted words are still in the manuscript (`r status_counts[["Open"]]`), the change covers only part of the entry (`r status_counts[["Partly resolved"]]`), or the entry quotes no words that can be searched for and must be checked by hand (`r status_counts[["Check by hand"]]`). The two tables below list them; the line numbers in the column "Where now" are those of the current manuscript, whereas the line numbers in the entries themselves are those of 1 November.

On 1 November 2026, most false statements had one of three roots. The first is **text that outlived the project stage it describes**: passages written for earlier versions of Metacheck or the earlier repository still describe files, reruns, sections and behaviour that no longer exist. This explains the paths to files that are not in this repository, the references to a "Coding section" and "Results", the naming rules that the module no longer has, and the crash that no longer occurs. The second is **a sentence that describes a broader pattern than its count supports**, such as a count of 55 papers described as all having the same cause when 27 do. The third is **a general statement that contradicts another part of the manuscript**: the Discussion says undetected repositories are overwhelmingly on Dryad, Zenodo or Figshare, whereas the Results, correctly, say they are mostly on platforms Metacheck does not support.

**The most consequential finding concerned a definition, and it has been acted on.** The manuscript called 294 README disagreements coder errors because no README file exists. Cooper et al. asked whether the data have a "README/metadata" and report a "README or equivalent" (p. 1960), so a coder who counted a description field answered the question as asked. On 1 November 2026 the author reclassified these 294 as `DIFFERENT_DEFINITION`, and the text was changed accordingly (entries C1.11, C12.4, C12.9, C16.7). The agreement percentages do not change. A second finding concerns the licence review: in four disagreements the comment does not support the verdict, although a check on the coded deposits suggests the verdict is right (entry C11.6).

```{r}
#| label: list-of-false
#| results: asis

cat("\n**Entries still open.** Each of these needs a change to the text or a decision.\n")
status_table(c("Open", "Partly resolved", "Check by hand"))
cat("\n**Entries settled since 1 November 2026.**\n")
status_table(c("Resolved", "Author's decision", "Statement removed", "Section removed", "Text removed or rewritten"))
```

# Part 1: Register of numbers

Each section below follows the manuscript's own sections. A section first explains what its numbers mean and how they are produced, and then lists every computed number with the words before it, the value the manuscript prints, the independently recomputed value, and whether they are the same. In the words before a number, the sign # stands for another computed number. Paper-level answers from Metacheck are produced by `recreate_cooper_columns()` and joined to Cooper et al.'s data by `build_cooper_vs_metacheck()` and `build_master_comparison()`; the statistics by `compute_comparison_statistics()`. All are defined in `code/R/` and run by `_targets.R`.

## Hackathon coding (Introduction)

*Definition.* The number of papers each of Cooper et al.'s 145 participants coded. *Provenance.* Column `recorder_ID` of `data/cooper_coded_data.csv`, carried into the target `master_comparison`. *Formula.* The median, minimum and maximum of the counts per value of `recorder_ID`. *Interpretation.* It shows how the work was divided: half of the participants coded at most 10 papers, and one coded 68.

```{r}
#| results: asis
num_table("Introduction")
```

## Text-based judgements of open data and code

*Definition.* How well two tools that read only the article's text agree with the coders' answer to whether archived data or code could be opened. OddPub (version 7.3.0, in `code/modules/`) and Metacheck's `open_practices` module each give TRUE or FALSE per paper. *Provenance.* `summary_table$data_open`, `code_open`, `data_open.oddpub` and `code_open.oddpub` of `data/metacheck_results.rds`, and columns `data_open` and `code_open` of Cooper et al.'s file. *Formula.* A coder answer of "Yes" counts as open, and for data also "Yes, but not all files"; "No" counts as not open; other answers and blanks are left out. Sensitivity is the share of open papers the tool calls open, specificity the share of not-open papers it calls not open, and accuracy the share of papers on which they agree. The second paragraph applies the tools to the papers left out: papers that archived data or code without an answer ("blank"), and papers with the answer "Needs specific software or too large" or "Maybe if I had the right software". *Interpretation.* The specificity values rest on 11 papers for data and 3 for code, so one paper moves the code value by 33 percentage points. These values should not be compared between tools.

```{r}
#| results: asis
num_table("Oddpub and Open Practices Check")
```

## Papers with data or code, and supported repositories

*Definition.* The first paragraph counts papers on each side. For Cooper et al., a paper counts when `data_availability` or `code_archived` is "Yes". For Metacheck, `n_mc_repo_found` counts papers with at least one listed file of any kind (`summary_table$files_n` above zero); `n_mc_data` counts papers with at least one file `data_check` classified as data; `n_mc_code` counts papers with at least one row in `code_check`'s table. *Formula.* Agreements and the two directions of disagreement are set operations on paper identifiers. *Interpretation.* The three Metacheck-side counts are nested differently from the Cooper-side counts: Cooper et al.'s "Yes" can rest on supporting information, whereas Metacheck requires a repository.

The second paragraph counts repositories from lists inside Metacheck (`.dataverse_hosts()`, `.dspace7_hosts()`, `.dspace_legacy_hosts()`, `.dataone_hosts()`, `.figshare_vanity_hosts()`, `.figshare_doi_prefix_hosts()`), plus 11, which is typed into the manuscript's code. **The Figshare count is wrong.** The manuscript takes `union(.figshare_vanity_hosts(), names(.figshare_doi_prefix_hosts()))`. The names of that second list are DOI prefixes (for example `10.17633`), and its values are hosts (for example `brunel.figshare.com`). The Dataverse list has it the other way round, with hosts as names, and this difference is the root of the error: code written for the Dataverse list was reused. The union therefore adds 35 prefixes to 41 hosts, giving 76, whereas the prefixes all point to hosts already counted. *Correction.* In `data-code-archiving-counts`, use `figshare_hosts <- union(metacheck:::.figshare_vanity_hosts(), unlist(metacheck:::.figshare_doi_prefix_hosts()))`, which gives 41 hosts and a total of 250. The 11 dedicated platforms are confirmed: each has its own functions in the package (C4.18).

```{r}
#| results: asis
num_table("Repo check, Data check, and Code check")
```

## Reasons Metacheck missed data or code (section 1, and table of reasons)

*Definition.* Each of the 274 papers where the coders found data or code and Metacheck found none has one row in `data/review/manual_repo_findability_audit_data.csv`, with a cause in `root_cause_category`, and one row in `manual_fair_api_findability_audit_data.csv`, with a judgement of whether the deposit is FAIR. *Formula.* The clusters are sums of categories, defined in chunk `full-317-audit-load`; they are mutually exclusive and the chunk stops if they do not add up to 274. "Not FAIR" papers are the 18 without a repository, the 16 whose format is not FAIR and the 81 with a link or repository that is not FAIR, 115 in total. The share of 90.5% is 1515 divided by 1789 minus 115. *Interpretation.* All of these numbers follow arithmetically from that one review. Their accuracy therefore rests on that review, in which each paper was read by one AI agent, with no second reader for most rows. No row was checked against the version of Metacheck in the final run: all 274 rows carry an earlier version (mostly 109a9aa or 610cd4f2), though the pipeline's target `audit_staleness` lists them for this purpose. Because the 274 are defined by the final run, the set of papers is current, but each explanation is as of its stated date.

These numbers appear in the manuscript under the heading "Repo check, Data check, and Code check" and are in the table above.

## Platforms and reuse (section 2)

*Definition.* Comparison of the set of platforms each side names per paper. Only papers where both sides name at least one platform are comparable. *Provenance.* `results$data_archive` and `results$code_archive`, from `platform_set_comparison()` in `code/R/platforms.R`. OSF on Metacheck's side and CRAN on Cooper et al.'s side are mapped to "Other repo/database", and "Supplementary materials" and "Personal website" are removed before the comparison. *Formula.* "Exact" means equal sets, "mc_fewer" means Metacheck's set is a strict subset, "mc_more" the reverse. The reuse numbers come from `data/review/github_repository_ownership_review_data.csv`. *Interpretation.* `n_github_repos` (215) and `n_third_party_repos` (31) count rows, each a pair of paper and repository, not distinct repositories: the distinct counts are 214 and 30 (entry C6.9).

```{r}
#| results: asis
num_table("2. Where were the data/code archived?")
```

## Downloads and code (section 3)

*Definition.* `n_dl_cooper_yes` counts papers whose `data_download` is "Yes" or "Yes, but not all data". `mc_data_download` is TRUE when at least one data file was saved and is usable as a table, FALSE when files were saved but none is usable, and missing when none was saved. *Provenance.* `recreate_cooper_columns()`; verdicts from `data/review/disagreement_review_data.xlsx`; the code categories from columns `code_category` and `code_category_reason` of the same file, which were entered by hand on 1 November 2026 for 203 rows. *Formula.* Agreement is the share of papers where both sides have an answer and the answers match. *Interpretation.* The agreement of 99.2% applies only to papers where Metacheck saved a file; counted over all papers the coders downloaded, the share is 83.6%, and the manuscript reports both. The numbers from `n_dl_right()` come from text patterns on review comments, and each was confirmed here by reading the comments (entries C7.6 to C7.8). The category counts rest on one reader's judgement of each paper.

```{r}
#| results: asis
num_table("3. Can the archived data/code be located, downloaded and opened?")
```

## Definitions of the columns

The only computed numbers here concern licence strings on Dryad. *Provenance.* `repo_check$repo_metadata`, reduced to one row per repository. *Formula.* Counts of repositories whose address is on Dryad and whose licence is the CC0 address. *Interpretation.* The count is by distinct repository (1058), whereas the raw table holds 1061 rows, because a repository cited by two papers has two rows.

## Data availability, licences and README (sections 5 and 6)

*Definition.* The confusion table of each comparison, from `compute_comparison_statistics()`: TP is Cooper "Yes" and Metacheck TRUE, FN is Cooper "Yes" and Metacheck FALSE, FP is Cooper "No" and Metacheck TRUE, TN is Cooper "No" and Metacheck FALSE. *Formula.* Agreement is the share of papers where both sides have an answer and the answers match; the review verdicts (manual coding correct, automatic coding correct, different definition, both defensible, both wrong) come from `data/review/disagreement_review_data.xlsx`. *Provenance of the causes.* `cooper_right_causes` assigns a review comment to the first matching group of text patterns (`categorize_disagreement_causes()`), so 175 and 96 are counts of wording, not of causes coded one by one. To test this, the 175 papers were matched to the audit of section 1: 122 of them are there classified as on a platform Metacheck does not support, which supports the manuscript's description in this section but contradicts the Discussion (entry C17.2). *Interpretation.* The agreement values and verdict counts measure agreement with the coders and the result of a by-hand review of each disagreement, not correctness by definition; the review found the coders wrong in many disagreements (for licences, the automatic coding was judged correct in 46 of 57). The numbers for these sections, including Table 4's columns, are listed under their manuscript headings in the completeness table below.
